title: Lakes Plain languages - Wikipedia
text: The Lakes Plain languages are a family of Papuan languages, spoken in the Lakes Plain of Indonesian New Guinea. They are notable for being heavily tonal and for their lack of nasal consonants.

title: Rasawa language — Grokipedia
text: Like other Lakes Plain languages, Rasawa is heavily tonal, with a core system of at least two level tones—high and low—associated with syllabic nuclei, a feature unusual among Papuan languages outside this family.
